name_full: d-APV (stored in the catalogue as D-Ap5)
label: Full competitive NMDA-receptor block, the reference control
action: Competitive block of the glutamate site: the control against which any negative modulator is read.
rationale: It abolishes the spontaneous bursts, so it bounds how much NMDA-receptor current must go before the burst stops.
open_premise: That the burst needs NMDA-receptor activity does not show a gain of receptor function.
counter: Against the wild-type floor about 20 percent of the delayed evoked response remains under it (figure-read, inference), which is not evidence of incomplete block.
next_test: Measure the abolition threshold (percent of isolated NMDA-receptor current removed) with measured bath magnesium; this is the first number every NAM comparison needs.
moves: A clean abolition threshold, measured on the isolated NMDA-receptor current, fixes the reference; nothing lowers it, it is the control.

label: Ifenprodil-site GluN2B negative modulator, used as a tool
action: Negative allosteric modulation of GluN2B-containing receptors at the ifenprodil site.
rationale: A burst effect at a smaller removed fraction than the control needs would make a GluN2B-directed comparison the better question.
open_premise: The removable share of such a modulator is bounded by receptor composition and zinc, so a plateau below the control is unresolved, not support for total gain.
counter: The compound's GluN2B rows are measured activities, not a curated mechanism, and other targets are also measured; selectivity is not assessed.
next_test: Measure its removable fraction in the isolated NMDA-receptor current first; compare with the control only up to that fraction. A second modulator of the same site controls chemotype only.
source_rows: nmda_composition D01-D03; identity_it41 (Harness); apply_inv05_delta; comparison_engine_it43 (tier PRIMARY)
moves: Up: a removable fraction at the burst clearly below the abolition threshold. Down: a plateau below the threshold, which stays unresolved rather than refuting the mechanism.

name_full: GYKI 53655; GYKI 52466 (a different structure, not the same compound); NBQX; perampanel
label: AMPA/kainate block arm: a pair of two mechanisms
action: Block of AMPA and kainate receptors with a noncompetitive 2,3-benzodiazepine and, as the independent partner, the competitive NBQX; perampanel shares the benzodiazepine's pocket and serves as a same-site cross-check.
rationale: Survival of the burst under a verified block would remove an AMPA contribution; abolition alone cannot separate AMPA drive from loss of magnesium relief.
open_premise: Whether an AMPA-dependent component exists at all; the 90 percent design value of the block is at the edge of what the tool gives in tissue (80-89 percent at 10 uM).
counter: The nearest tissue precedent, evoked Up states of barrel cortex, persisted under the benzodiazepine (transfer, with limits); two compounds are registered under one GYKI label; kainate is not separated.
next_test: Measure the achieved block and the NMDA-receptor current at the working concentration; test survival of the bursts under a verified block; d-APV only if bursts persist.
moves: Up for the survival question: bursts persisting under a verified block. Down: abolition, which does not separate the explanations.

label: Ih (HCN) blocker as a tool arm, after matched-condition recordings
action: Block of the hyperpolarisation-activated current, two chemotypes, engagement shown first.
rationale: Only worth running if sag and rebound stay larger at matched potential and deflection.
open_premise: Whether any HCN contribution remains after matching; no benefit is claimed.
counter: A blocker response shows contribution as in normal cortex, not a defect; the passive-size reading is the rival; a sodium-current block is reported for one tool in thalamic neurons (abstract level).
next_test: Run the matched-condition recording with capacitance and access resistance first; no HCN compound is nominated before it.
moves: Up: the excess sag persisting at matched potential and deflection. Down: it vanishing, or the blocker-sensitive current per capacitance being the same.

label: Clinical-stage GluN2B negative modulator with an assembly-dependent maximum
action: Negative modulation of GluN2B-containing receptors; maximum inhibition 82 percent on rat GluN1/GluN2B against 45 percent on rat triheteromers (human GluN1/GluN2B 91 percent).
rationale: A clinical-stage compound (catalogue maximum phase 2) that could serve as the in-slice modulator once the tool result is in.
open_premise: That the ceiling seen in oocytes holds in the slice; its washout is very slow in oocytes.
counter: The selectivity statement rests on a supplementary figure that was not read; slice precedent is a different region and age.
next_test: Use only after V02 shows a removable fraction; read the fraction at the burst, not in oocytes.
moves: Up: a removable fraction already shown by the tool. Down: a ceiling like the tool's, which adds a chemotype and nothing else.

label: Human-exposure GluN2B negative modulator; site, maximum effect and triheteromer behaviour not measured in any source reached
action: Negative modulation of the GluN2B subunit; the receptor site is not recorded.
rationale: A second scaffold (sharing a structural arrangement with ifenprodil-type ligands: inference from structure) read after the ifenprodil-site tool, to ask whether a different scaffold removes the same measured percent of the isolated NMDA-receptor current.
open_premise: Whether it shares the ifenprodil site and the triheteromer ceiling; the registry gives no receptor site.
counter: Two sponsor-authored clinical papers read at partial full text; the only potency is one patent calcium-flux IC50 (8.3 nM) on NR1/NR2B cells without Mg2+, with no stated Zn2+ chelator or pH.
next_test: None found by open routes (a patent and two clinical papers read; an analogue paper not reached); the measurement is the removable fraction in the isolated NMDA-receptor current, after the ifenprodil-site tool.
registry_note: Registry (GtoPdb 2026.3.1) row: human GluN2B, negative allosteric modulator, pIC50 8.08 (the 8.3 in the original-affinity field is the same datum as an IC50 in nM), sourced to a patent, selectivity not determined, no assay text and no receptor site. One applicant measurement copied into BindingDB, ChEMBL and GtoPdb (the GtoPdb link is by value identity); the patent assay has no maximum effect.
moves: Up: a primary source placing it at the ifenprodil site with a clearly different triheteromer maximum, or at a different documented site that gives a different comparison. Down: none reached; it stays a conditional second scaffold after the tool.

label: pH-dependent GluN2B modulator: a pH-linked comparison, subordinate to a measured tissue pH; not a candidate
action: Inhibition of GluN2B-containing receptors, stronger at acidic pH.
rationale: Potency is pH-dependent (declared about 6-fold; IC50 21 and 130 nM at pH 6.9 and 7.6, abstract level, same developer); for the series prototype the maximum moved little (76 to 83 percent, measured in oocytes).
open_premise: The pH of the recorded tissue is unmeasured; ifenprodil may itself be pH-sensitive (older abstracts) and a related clinical-stage modulator is declared not to be (a 2015 table not read).
counter: Phase 1 in healthy adults (partial full text); maximum effect, site, triheteromer and slice data absent; H1 and hERG actions declared.
next_test: Measure the tissue pH; if this compound is used, run the ifenprodil-site tool and the full competitive antagonist at the same two controlled pH values, with its recombinant maximum at each pH known first.
registry_note: Registry (GtoPdb 2026.3.1) row: inhibition of human GluN2B in oocytes at pH 6.9, pIC50 7.64, selectivity not determined; the registry flags the compound as approved while ChEMBL gives maximum phase 1 (the flag is not carried). GtoPdb's approved flag conflicts with ChEMBL and the abstract (maximum phase 1); the value 7.64 is probably the same measurement as 21 nM (inference).
moves: Up: a measured tissue pH in the range where the dependence is large, with a drug-by-pH interaction larger than for the ifenprodil-site tool and the full antagonist at the same two pH values. Down: a tissue pH near physiological, or an interaction not larger than theirs. A burst effect that follows the pH is not a specificity signature.

label: Class recorded on a GluN1/GluN2B assembly record, no maximum effect
action: Antagonism recorded on the two-gene GRIN1/GRIN2B record of a curated mechanism table.
rationale: Possible chemotype controls if V02 and V05 do not give one.
open_premise: That an assembly record means subunit selectivity: it names where the mechanism was attached, not how selective the molecule is.
counter: No maximum effect, species or assay context in the catalogue; no approval statement in the catalogue. A second ifenprodil-site tool, moved here from the tool entry: only abstract-level values were reached and its triheteromer behaviour is transferred from another compound, so it is not a tool for this comparison until its primary source is read.
next_test: Read primary sources for maximum effect and site only if a further chemotype is needed. For that second tool the first step is reading its primary source; no new measurement is needed for that.
registry_note: Registry (ChEMBL 37) curated mechanism rows: antagonist on the record GRIN1/GRIN2B (two genes), maximum phase 2 or lower.
moves: Up: a primary source giving site and maximum effect. Down: nothing needed unless the tool and the clinical-stage compound do not give a chemotype control.

label: The registry GluN2B row is a GluN2B measurement (113 micromolar) stored as nanomolar; DQP-1105 prefers GluN2C and GluN2D: excluded from the GluN2B comparison
action: Recorded as a negative modulator under a GluN2B entry.
open_premise: Resolved at source: the paper's table gives GluN2B 113, GluN2C 7.0 and GluN2D 2.7 micromolar; the registry rows for GluN2B and GluN2C hold micromolar numbers entered as nanomolar (inference for the cause, data for the identity of the numbers).
counter: No maximum per subunit is reported; the GluN2B value is a fitted IC50 with complete inhibition assumed. A registry value under a target can fail by unit, not only by subunit.
next_test: None; kept so the filing is not mistaken for evidence: the registry row is not evidence of GluN2B potency in nanomolar.
registry_note: Registry (GtoPdb 2026.3.1) rows under GluN2B (pIC50 6.95) and GluN2C (8.15) are pIC50 values computed from micromolar numbers entered as nanomolar (a thousand-fold; about 3.95 and 5.15 expected); the GluN2D row is correct. The assay text of the GluN2B row names GluN2C.
moves: Nothing moves it: kept so the filing is not mistaken for evidence. Reopen if the primary paper assigns the value to GluN2B.

label: Kv7 opening and gap-junction block: abstain
action: Opening of Kv7 channels, or block of connexin and pannexin channels, proposed in earlier readings.
rationale: A response would not show a defect of the target in these cells.
open_premise: That a leak deficit or coupling drives the burst: neither is shown; the burst fall under the gap-junction tool has no supporting datum for coupling. Kv7 current starts near −70 mV, so an opener's expected action is in the spiking range, not at the Wwox rest.
counter: Smaller cells with a seal leak, and effects on synaptic currents seen in culture, would give the same observations.
next_test: Nominate nothing before a Ba2+- or XE-991-sensitive difference current smaller per pF in Wwox neurons with capacitance measured directly and the junction potential measured; a reversal near E_K alone does not separate a K+ loss from a smaller cell with a shunt; a matched-effect control that fails to reproduce the fall.
moves: Up: a difference current reversing near the potassium equilibrium potential in Wwox neurons, and a matched-effect control that fails to reproduce the fall. Down: passive size with a seal leak explaining the observations. Down: a smaller cell with a shunt gives the same implied reversal.

name_full: tiagabine; NNC-711; other selective GAT-1 inhibitors as tools
label: Supply-side GABA lever: block of GABA reuptake, a different question from receptor potentiation
action: Block of the GABA transporter GAT-1 raises GABA availability without touching glutamate-receptor currents; the catalogue records maximum phase 4 for one reference compound and lists several selective tools.
rationale: It separates a deficit of GABA supply from a postsynaptic or chloride-gradient deficit: only the first is helped by more GABA.
open_premise: Whether the halved inhibitory current is a supply deficit; the direction depends on the chloride gradient of the preparation, which is unmeasured.
counter: In the repository's own records raising GABAergic tone is unresolved (an irreversible inactivator of GABA transaminase resolved spasms in one of two children, partly in the other, with null reports elsewhere, and carries a brain-imaging signal); a compensatory change in tonic inhibition or transporter expression could mask the effect.
next_test: Re-record the sIPSC under glutamate block with a fixed threshold and per-animal summary first, then E_GABA by gramicidin perforated patch in littermates, then the age series; the lever, against a GABA-A potentiator and a non-GABAergic suppression matched to the same measured effect, only after these.
moves: Up: a low evoked IPSC with a hyperpolarising chloride gradient and a lever effect above the matched non-GABAergic control. Down: a response-side deficit, or depolarising GABA.

label: GABA-transaminase block: affinities of irreversible inhibitors are not a potency ranking
action: Inactivation of GABA transaminase raises GABA; the registry rows are affinity values for compounds that act irreversibly.
rationale: It is the other way to raise GABA availability, kept so that the two ways are not mixed.
open_premise: That a lower affinity number means a weaker compound: for irreversible inactivators the number does not measure it.
counter: The repository already records that the older drug resolved spasms in one child and carries a brain-imaging safety signal; the newer one is clinical-stage only (catalogue maximum phase 1).
next_test: No comparison before an inactivation parameter is available; start from the supply-side question of V11.
registry_note: Registry (GtoPdb 2026.3.1) rows on human ABAT: pKi 3.07 for the older drug (labelled irreversible inhibition) and pKi 5.01 for the newer one (labelled inhibition); 4-acryloylphenol has a pIC50 and its primary target in the registry is another enzyme (ABAT is non-primary). The values are not a potency ranking of irreversible inactivators.
moves: Nothing moves it until an inactivation measure exists; then up if the newer compound shows a clearly larger inactivation rate under the same assay.

label: Lowering the kinases that restrain the pyruvate dehydrogenase step: a carded lever with typed, per-isoform rows, conditional on an unmeasured premise; the first probe depends on the dominant kinase of the cell class and on the assay scaffold
action: Inhibition of the pyruvate dehydrogenase kinases, releasing the dehydrogenase step so more pyruvate is oxidised.
rationale: The lever was already carded; the search now gives a reference and a second, unrelated chemotype with rows on each kinase isoform, so a first experiment can compare them once the premise holds.
open_premise: That the dehydrogenase step is actually restrained in a WWOX-deficient human neural cell, per cell class: no neural measurement of its amount, phosphorylation or activity exists, the dominant kinase differs by class and species, and the signs conflict (a lower kinase transcript in an organoid; a higher one with unchanged activity in a non-neural fibroblast line).
counter: The reference has a family record only; the two others rest on one assay each; one of them is an activator when the assay lacks the scaffold core and an inhibitor when it has it; two isoforms have no row for one compound (unknown, not zero). Lowering the kinases is also a risk arm: harm directions are documented (a proconvulsant effect at abstract level, benefit only for a combination in a rat seizure model, a fall of peripheral myelin proteins, nerve toxicity in the one randomised human trial) and a lactate-supply role makes the net direction by class unknown. Nothing is known about brain exposure.
next_test: Premise measurement per cell class on sorted or marker-resolved material, with a genetic knockdown of the dominant isoform first; compare the reference with the second chemotype only if a restraint is measured.
registry_note: Registry rows: ChEMBL mechanism (inhibitor, family record); GtoPdb inhibitor rows with pIC50 per isoform from two assays. AZD7545: the species recorded as human is not supported by its abstract (rat-indexed) and the 2003 primary was not reached; core-bound inhibition (PDK1, PDK3) versus core-free stimulation (PDK3, PDK4) in a later paper. VER-246608: Table 1 IC50 values reproduce the pIC50 rows (E1-only assay, species not named). The reference is a millimolar inhibitor and isoform-dependent.
moves: Up: a measured restraint of the step. Down: none found, which lowers the lead without refuting it in other cell types. Reopens with the opposite sign if the cells depend on lactate supply.

name_full: riluzole; BL-1249; flufenamic acid (K2P-type openers); zacopride (Kir2.1 opener)
label: Adding a resting K+ conductance with an opener: the openers that exist act on the weakly Ba2+-sensitive channel family
action: Opening of K2P-type (TREK, TRAAK) or Kir2-type channels to restore a resting K+ conductance.
rationale: The action was named without a compound; the search shows catalogued openers exist for the K2P family, so the question becomes whether a lost current would be of that family.
open_premise: That the lost current, if any, is Ba2+-sensitive and of a family an opener reaches: TREK and TRAAK are blocked only at millimolar Ba2+, and the one Kir2 opener reached is Kir2.1-only with no neuronal data; capacitance by genotype is unmeasured.
counter: The glutamate-release modulator active on K2P channels also blocks sodium channels and glutamate release at lower concentrations and needs about 100 micromolar for the K2P effect; its activation of one family member is transient; some potencies rest on a review, not a primary paper; selectivity of the research activator against other channels is not fully reached.
next_test: Measure capacitance, then the Ba2+-sensitive current per pF at a low and a high Ba2+ concentration; only a current blocked by low micromolar Ba2+ points to Kir-type channels; compare an opener with a blocker only after that.
registry_note: Registry: GtoPdb activator rows on the K2P family, ChEMBL activity rows on TREK-1 from a review document; Kir2: PIP2 only (physiological).
moves: Up: a current blocked at low micromolar Ba2+ and smaller per pF in the mutant (the opener route is then narrow). Down: a Ba2+-sensitive share only at millimolar concentrations, equal per pF, or a lower capacitance with flat time constant.

label: A lactate-side probe: the sign depends on the cell compartment
action: Inhibition of lactate dehydrogenase to lower lactate production, as a probe of the supply side of the same metabolic node.
rationale: A lever on the other side of the node from the kinase: if lactate supply to neurons matters, lowering it could help or harm depending on the compartment.
open_premise: That lactate is raised in the knockout slice and that the burst needs lactate supply: neither is measured.
counter: The evidence is outside WWOX (adult mouse status epilepticus and slice activity); resting properties were never measured; the comparator has a mixed mechanism (GABA-A potentiation) and its enzyme value is copied from a review; no typed catalogue row exists for the enzyme, so the search by symbol reaches nothing.
next_test: Measure lactate and pyruvate in the slice with the premise series; only then a matched-suppression comparison against a non-metabolic route.
registry_note: No typed ChEMBL or GtoPdb row for LDHA/LDHB; two DGIdb listings (a class label and a code).
moves: Up: lactate raised in the knockout and a burst fall that tracks lactate supply. Down: lactate unchanged, or a fall explained by GABA-A potentiation or pH.

label: A probe at the opposite end of the node and a fuel control, to separate a dehydrogenase defect from a supply defect
action: Block of mitochondrial pyruvate entry as a probe, and an alternative fuel that bypasses the dehydrogenase step as a control.
rationale: Activity alone cannot separate a restrained dehydrogenase step from a supply problem; a fuel that bypasses the step and a block of entry give the two opposite expectations.
open_premise: That any WWOX preparation shows a restraint or a supply defect; the direction label of the entry block is an inference.
counter: Neuronal culture and epileptic-mouse data only; protection by the entry block is not benefit; the fuel's effect was measured as enzyme activity, not flux.
next_test: Run both with the premise series: a fuel that restores function points to supply; an entry block that protects points away from release of the dehydrogenase step.
registry_note: Pyruvate-entry blocker typed in GtoPdb only (a name-route gap in the identity join); the fuel is a catalogue record.
moves: Up: function restored by the fuel but not by kinase inhibition. Down: no change with the fuel in cells where the step is unrestrained.

label: ATP-sensitive K+ channel tools: a conditional metabolic upstream of the potassium branch
action: Open or occlude ATP-sensitive K+ channels to test whether a lactate-closed resting conductance contributes to input resistance.
rationale: In juvenile barrel cortex these channels change membrane potential, input resistance and firing, and lactate can close them: a metabolic upstream of the resting-conductance question, capped at about half of the implied loss.
open_premise: The pipette ATP and bath glucose of the recordings, and whether lactate is raised in the knockout slice; whole-cell dialysis can mask the effect.
counter: One verifier-read source; the pyramidal share of the pooled cells is inferred; no Wwox neuron has been tested.
next_test: Add a perforated or cell-attached arm with ATP undisturbed to the potassium ladder, with an opener, a sulfonylurea and lactate or pyruvate add-back, stating pipette ATP and glucose.
registry_note: Reached by the unchanged relation path (ChEMBL mechanism and GtoPdb rows).
moves: Up: an opener-sensitive and sulfonylurea-occluded current smaller per pF in the mutant. Down: no difference with ATP undisturbed.
